faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Rocket Motor Case suitable for Solid rocket motor case section ring?
faq.a: Titanium Rocket Motor Case uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address missile hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Rocket Motor Case?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Rocket Motor Case is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for solid rocket motor requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Rocket Motor Case require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. solid rocket motor components require Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for solid rocket motor application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Rocket Motor Case shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Rocket Motor Case includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet solid rocket motor specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
